19-02-opti-1: Kennedy Space Center, in Florida. A rocket roars into the night.
19-02-opti-2: It carries supplies to the space station, high above Earth.
19-02-opti-3: Inside, something is growing in a strange pink glow...
19-02-opti-5: First, tiny sprouts. And not one ray of sunshine.
19-02-opti-6: Bright lamps shine all day. Four weeks later, the lettuce is ready to eat!
19-02-opti-7: Back in Florida, scientists test one light at a time.
19-02-opti-8: So does light really matter? Let's find out.
19-02-welcome: Today's film goes all the way to space! First, look closely at some sprouts that grew without any sunlight.
19-02-lesson: Today you're the crew's plant tester. Run a fair test, cover plants in the Light Lab, and dive down to find where plants stop growing.
19-02-assign: Time to build your graph. Let the numbers tell you what light does to a plant.
19-02-words: Data. Graph. Pattern. Evidence. Condition. Growth rate.
how-19-02-compare: Put the clear cup over one tray and the cardboard box over the other: drag them, or tap each one, then tap a tray. Press Let seven days pass. Then swap them and press it again.
how-19-02-partc: Draw both plants as they looked on Day seven. Label the height of each one, and write its light condition next to it.
how-19-02-write: What does your investigation tell you about how light affects plant growth? Answer the three questions. Use all three of the science words under the boxes.
19-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
